did_you_know.text: Did you know? On the twenty-fourth day of the month, the Israelites gathered in fasting, wearing sackcloth and with dust on their heads as an expression of mourning and repentance.
Did you know? The daily schedule included reading from the Book of the Law of the LORD for one-quarter of the day, followed by confession and worship for another quarter of the day.
Did you know? The prayer describes the LORD as the Creator of the heavens, the earth, the seas, and everything in them—and as the One who gives life to all living things.
Did you know? The prayer recalls that the LORD found Abraham’s heart faithful to Him, made a covenant with him, and promised the land to his descendants.
Did you know? In the wilderness, the LORD led Israel with a pillar of cloud by day and a pillar of fire by night to guide them and light their way.
Did you know? Among the gifts given to Israel in the wilderness was instruction about the holy Sabbath, along with the commandments and laws given through Moses.
Did you know? During the forty years of wandering in the wilderness, the Israelites lacked nothing: their clothes did not wear out, and their feet did not swell.
Did you know? After entering the land, the Israelites experienced material prosperity: fortified cities, houses filled with good things, cisterns, vineyards, olive trees, and other fruit trees.
Did you know? The chapter describes a recurring cycle: sin and rebellion, being handed over to enemies, crying out to the LORD, and the sending of deliverers to rescue them in His mercy.

Did you know? In the prayer, the people acknowledge that the LORD is righteous in all that has happened to them and note that their troubles have continued from the days of the kings of Assyria until their own time.
